The maintained replication code behind these errata is at <https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_green_2022> and is archived at Zenodo at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24168344>, a DOI that always resolves to the latest version.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

out <- function(file) {
  read_csv(here("maintained", "output", file), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

pwa <- out("text_precision_weighted_averages.csv")
ranges <- out("text_precision_weighted_averages_endpoint_ranges.csv")
pooled <- out("text_pooled_ratio_metaanalysis.csv")
dispersion <- out("text_pooled_ratio_dispersion.csv")
t1 <- out("table_1_static_constraint_correlations.csv")
t2 <- out("table_2_employment_discrimination.csv")
t3 <- out("table_3_inequality.csv")
t4 <- out("table_4_correction_experiment.csv")
b2 <- out("table_b2_sample_demographics.csv")
inconsistency <- out("text_inconsistency_rates.csv")
descriptions <- out("text_sample_descriptions.csv")
# Entry 11's two p-values, read from Table C.4's own output so the note cannot
# assert a threshold the table does not support.
c4_ineq <- out("table_c4_welfare_experiment.csv") |>
  filter(outcome == "Gov Should Reduce Ineq", term == "Welfare wording")
stopifnot(nrow(c4_ineq) == 2, all(c4_ineq$p.value > 0.05))
c4_ineq_p <- set_names(c4_ineq$p.value, c4_ineq$sample)

archive <- read_csv(here("ground_truth", "archive_values.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

r0 <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f", x)
r1 <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
r2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
r3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)

# spell: two of the corrected sentences replace a number the article spells out,
# and a numeral in place of a word would not be a minimal edit.
spell <- function(n) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight",
             "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve")
  stopifnot(n >= 1, n <= length(words), n == round(n))
  words[n]
}

fe <- pooled |> filter(model == "Fixed effects")
pooled_estimate <- 100 * fe$estimate
pooled_low <- 100 * fe$conf_low
pooled_high <- 100 * fe$conf_high
# The deposit's own ideology table carries rows with no label, so archive$term has
# NAs and a bare logical subset returns them alongside the value asked for.
archive_value <- function(term_name) {
  value <- archive |> filter(term == term_name) |> pull(value)
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1, !is.na(value))
  value
}

archive_pooled <- 100 * archive_value("Pooled indirect-to-direct ratio")

ratio <- function(sample_name, column) {
  100 * pwa[[column]][pwa$sample == sample_name & pwa$quantity == "ratio"]
}

endpoint_range <- function(sample_name, endpoint_name, sims) {
  row <- ranges |>
    filter(sample == sample_name, quantity == "ratio", endpoint == endpoint_name,
           sims_setting == sims)
  c(low = 100 * row$mc_low, high = 100 * row$mc_high)
}

lucid_high <- ratio("Lucid", "conf_high")
lucid_high_10 <- endpoint_range("Lucid", "conf_high", 10)
lucid_high_1000 <- endpoint_range("Lucid", "conf_high", 1000)
lucid_low_10 <- endpoint_range("Lucid", "conf_low", 10)

pooled_range <- function(quantity_name, sims) {
  row <- dispersion |> filter(quantity == quantity_name, sims_setting == sims)
  c(low = 100 * row$mc_low, high = 100 * row$mc_high)
}

pooled_estimate_10 <- pooled_range("estimate", 10)

mturk_within <- t1$within_domain[t1$sample == "MTurk sample"]

share <- function(sample_name, quantity_name) {
  row <- descriptions |> filter(sample == sample_name, quantity == quantity_name)
  100 * row$n_yes / row$n_sample
}

n_nontarget_s2 <- n_distinct(t2$outcome) - 1

study_2_cors <- out("text_study_2_correlations.csv")
s2_original_cors <- study_2_cors$correlation[study_2_cors$sample == "Original"]

esj_se <- t3$std.error[t3$sample == "Replication" & t3$term == "Inequality treatment" &
                         str_starts(t3$outcome, "Econ")]

correction <- function(sample_name) {
  t4$estimate[t4$sample == sample_name & t4$gov_pref == "Prefer small government" &
                t4$term == "Correction treatment"]
}

inconsistent <- function(sample_name) {
  100 * inconsistency$share_inconsistent[inconsistency$sample == sample_name]
}
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from here: into this
# document, and into whatever else needs it, which reads the errata_entries.csv written at
# the bottom of this file rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes, on both sides. Each renderer supplies its own markup
# for it, and this document's convention is to bold the corrected side only, so the marks
# on the published side are stripped rather than set. Nothing else in a field is markup.
# Numbers that move without being at issue are recomputed and left unmarked, which is why
# entries 3 and 8 carry corrected figures outside the marked spans.
#
# Numbering is positional (severity blocks, PROCEDURES.md Stage 4b; renumbered 2026-11-07) and these entries may be renumbered. Alex, 2026-08-14, asked
# whether an entry that turned out to be wrong should be withdrawn at its number or simply
# removed: "dont worry about the numbering, nobody's citing this yet, we're just working in
# public." So a wrong entry is deleted and the rest close up. An entry that corrected an
# endpoint the article never printed was removed on that instruction, and the finding behind
# it is in the README under "That endpoint was misread here, not misprinted there" and in
# notes.md. When these notes start being cited, appending becomes the only safe order again.
#
# claim_ids names the ground-truth rows an entry corrects, semicolon-separated, so that
# "is this finding published?" is a query rather than a judgment. It lists only the rows
# whose values the entry actually changes: entries 7 and 9 change no recorded quantity and
# name none. Every id listed is checked against the ground truth by build_ground_truth.R.
#
# corrected_values runs parallel to claim_ids, one value per id in the same order, carrying
# the corrected quantity as a number rather than as a sentence. The sentence already holds
# it, but only inside prose a reader has to parse: entry 3's marked span reads "four" and
# entry 5's reads "72%". in_text_claims.R asserts that the value it computes for a corrected
# claim is this one, which is the check that the correction this note publishes is the
# correction the pipeline currently supports. Each value comes from the same expression that
# glues the sentence, so the two cannot be written apart, and the gate below re-checks that
# each one is still inside the span it belongs to. A class that changes no quantity carries
# NA here, and so does an entry that names no claim.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The sign of the pooled ratio",
  "main text",
  "If we pool the three studies together, our estimate is [[1.4%]] (95% CI: -8%, 6%).",
  str_glue("If we pool the three studies together, our estimate is [[{r1(pooled_estimate)}%]] (95% CI: -8%, 6%)."),
  str_glue(
    "The three inputs are the sample-specific ratios of the precision-weighted average ",
    "nontarget effect to the precision-weighted average target effect: ",
    "{r1(ratio('MTurk', 'estimate'))}% on MTurk, {r1(ratio('Elite', 'estimate'))}% among ",
    "elites and {r1(ratio('Lucid', 'estimate'))}% on Lucid. The deposited ",
    "`in_text_numbers.R` pools them with `rmeta::meta.summaries`, which passes no `method` ",
    "argument and is therefore an inverse-variance fixed-effect meta-analysis. Two of the ",
    "three inputs are near zero and the third is negative with the second-smallest standard ",
    "error, so no pooling at these weights can land above zero; running the deposited code ",
    "today gives {r1(archive_pooled)}%. The published interval endpoints are left as printed ",
    "because they fall inside the range the unseeded bootstrap produces, which the point ",
    "estimate does not: over repeated runs at the resample count the deposit ships, the ",
    "pooled estimate lies between {r1(pooled_estimate_10['low'])}% and ",
    "{r1(pooled_estimate_10['high'])}%."),
  "s1_ratio_pooled", r1(pooled_estimate),

  2, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The same ratio in the discussion",
  "discussion",
  "But in only nine of 144 opportunities did it induce significant changes on nontarget issues, and the average spillover effect is just [[1.4%]] of the first-stage direct effect.",
  str_glue("But in only nine of 144 opportunities did it induce significant changes on nontarget issues, and the average spillover effect is just [[{r1(pooled_estimate)}%]] of the first-stage direct effect."),
  "The same quantity as item 1, restated. The counts in the sentence are correct.",
  "disc_spillover_ratio", r1(pooled_estimate),

  3, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The number of nontarget questions in study 2",
  "main text",
  "Responses to these nontarget outcomes are positively correlated among each other and with the target outcome of the manipulation (correlations range from 0.3 to 0.7), so it is reasonable to imagine that subjects would apply the religious conviction consideration when answering the [[three]] further questions.",
  str_glue("Responses to these nontarget outcomes are positively correlated among each other and with the target outcome of the manipulation (correlations range from 0.3 to 0.7), so it is reasonable to imagine that subjects would apply the religious conviction consideration when answering the [[{spell(n_nontarget_s2)}]] further questions."),
  str_glue(
    "Table 2 reports {spell(n_nontarget_s2)} nontarget outcomes, and the results paragraph ",
    "two paragraphs later calls them \"the four additional outcome measures\". The design ",
    "sentence before this one groups them into three topics rather than counting the ",
    "questions, describing one measure that raises the religious objection in another domain ",
    "and \"the other two outcome measures\" covering same-sex marriage and school prayer; ",
    "school prayer is measured with two questions, not one. The stated correlation range is ",
    "correct: the {spell(length(s2_original_cors))} pairwise correlations in the original ",
    "sample run from {r2(min(s2_original_cors))} to {r2(max(s2_original_cors))}."),
  "s2_nontarget_measures_text", as.character(n_nontarget_s2),

  4, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The MTurk within-domain correlation",
  "main text",
  "On MTurk, the average correlation between attitudes in the same domain was smaller at [[0.29]], and the average correlation between attitudes in different domains was very small at 0.06.",
  str_glue("On MTurk, the average correlation between attitudes in the same domain was smaller at [[{r2(mturk_within)}]], and the average correlation between attitudes in different domains was very small at 0.06."),
  str_glue(
    "The quantity is {sprintf('%.4f', mturk_within)}. Table 1 prints .30 for it, so the ",
    "table rounds it correctly and the sentence does not."),
  "s1_mturk_within_text", r2(mturk_within),

  5, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The graduate degree shares",
  "main text",
  "A full 96% of the elite sample hold a college degree, compared with 51% of the MTurk sample and 44% of the Lucid sample; [[71%]] of the elites hold a graduate degree, compared with [[13%]] for the MTurk sample and 15% for Lucid.",
  str_glue("A full 96% of the elite sample hold a college degree, compared with 51% of the MTurk sample and 44% of the Lucid sample; [[{r0(share('Elite', 'Graduate degree'))}%]] of the elites hold a graduate degree, compared with [[{r0(share('MTurk', 'Graduate degree'))}%]] for the MTurk sample and 15% for Lucid."),
  str_glue(
    "Appendix table B.2 prints {sprintf('%.1f', share('Elite', 'Graduate degree'))}% and ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', share('MTurk', 'Graduate degree'))}% for the same two categories, so ",
    "the sentence truncates the first and rounds the second the wrong way. The three ",
    "college-degree shares, which appear in no table, are ",
    "{r1(share('Elite', 'College degree or more'))}%, ",
    "{r1(share('MTurk', 'College degree or more'))}% and ",
    "{r1(share('Lucid', 'College degree or more'))}% and hold as printed."),
  "s1_graduate_elite;s1_graduate_mturk",
  str_c(r0(share("Elite", "Graduate degree")), ";", r0(share("MTurk", "Graduate degree"))),

  6, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "A standard error in study 3",
  "main text",
  "By contrast, the effects on economic system justification are small and close to zero: -0.18 standard units in the original study (SE: 0.10) and -0.07 units in the replication (SE: [[0.06]]).",
  str_glue("By contrast, the effects on economic system justification are small and close to zero: -0.18 standard units in the original study (SE: 0.10) and -0.07 units in the replication (SE: [[{r2(esj_se)}]])."),
  str_glue(
    "Table 3 prints {r3(esj_se)} for the same standard error. As in item 5, the sentence ",
    "truncates where the table rounds."),
  "s3_esj_replication_se", r2(esj_se),

  7, "label", "pipeline", "full",
  "The sample the inconsistency rates come from",
  "main text",
  "As is well documented (Ahler and Broockman 2018; Sears and Citrin 1982), inconsistency between preferences for smaller government and increased social spending is common. Among the [[MTurk]] sample, 30% of the respondents were inconsistent; this figure was 24% [[on Lucid]].",
  str_glue("As is well documented (Ahler and Broockman 2018; Sears and Citrin 1982), inconsistency between preferences for smaller government and increased social spending is common. Among the [[study 2 original]] sample, {r0(inconsistent('Original'))}% of the respondents were inconsistent; this figure was {r0(inconsistent('Replication'))}% [[in the replication]]."),
  str_glue(
    "Both figures come from study 2, and both study 2 samples were recruited on Lucid: the ",
    "body text says the 1,087 subjects for that experiment \"were also recruited via ",
    "Lucid\", and appendix table C.3 heads its two columns \"Lucid Original\" and \"Lucid ",
    "Replication\". The indicator that defines inconsistency appears in no MTurk data file ",
    "in the deposit. Table 4 carries the same mislabel in its row heading \"N (MTurk)\"; its ",
    "cells are correct and it is not reprinted here."),
  "disc_inconsistent_sample_label", NA_character_,

  8, "label", "pipeline", "full",
  "The sample the correction effects come from",
  "main text",
  "The results are shown in table 4. When induced to become more consistent, people who prefer smaller government prefer less spending (-0.172 scale points [[on MTurk]], -0.153 scale points [[on Lucid]]).",
  str_glue("The results are shown in table 4. When induced to become more consistent, people who prefer smaller government prefer less spending ({r3(correction('Original'))} scale points [[in the original Lucid sample]], {r3(correction('Replication'))} scale points [[in the Lucid replication]])."),
  str_glue(
    "The same mislabel as item 7. Table 4's top panel is fitted on the study 2 original ",
    "sample, the same 1,087 Lucid respondents table 2's top panel uses and appendix table ",
    "C.3's first column describes."),
  "disc_correction_sample_label", NA_character_,

  9, "cross_reference", "reading", "full",
  "The figures section B.4 does not name",
  "app. Section B.4",
  "[[Figures]] show that while the treatment effects on target issues remain significant even a full month after treatment, the effects on nontarget issues remain very close to zero over time.",
  "[[Figures B.2 and B.3]] show that while the treatment effects on target issues remain significant even a full month after treatment, the effects on nontarget issues remain very close to zero over time.",
  str_glue(
    "The sentence refers to figures and names none. Section B.4 has exactly two, and they are ",
    "the two the sentence describes: Figure B.2 gives the estimates ten days after treatment ",
    "and Figure B.3 the estimates thirty days after, which is the full month the sentence ",
    "appeals to. The omission is in the authors' own appendix source as well as on the ",
    "published page, and the two numbers are the only words this adds."),
  NA_character_, NA_character_,

  10, "cross_reference", "reading", "full",
  "The table section A.2 cites for the 32 graphs",
  "app. Section A.2",
  "These three edges blow up the possible number of graphs from the 32 in [[Table 1]] to 256.",
  "These three edges blow up the possible number of graphs from the 32 in [[Table A.1]] to 256.",
  str_glue(
    "The 32 graphs are enumerated in appendix Table A.1. Table 1 of the article reports levels ",
    "of static constraint and enumerates nothing. The count is right and the reference points ",
    "at the wrong table; as with entry 9, the slip is in the authors' own appendix source as ",
    "well as on the published page."),
  NA_character_, NA_character_,

  11, "wording", "reading", "full",
  "A significance threshold stated as a percentage",
  "app. Section C.2",
  "The effect of the prime on subsequent support for government reducing income gaps is slightly negative and is not significant at the [[0.05%]] level in either sample.",
  "The effect of the prime on subsequent support for government reducing income gaps is slightly negative and is not significant at the [[0.05]] level in either sample.",
  str_glue(
    "The article's tables mark significance at p < .05 throughout, and a 0.05% level would be ",
    "p < .0005, a threshold the article uses nowhere. The claim the sentence makes holds at the ",
    "0.05 level: Table C.4 gives p = {r3(c4_ineq_p['Original'])} in the original sample and ",
    "p = {r3(c4_ineq_p['Replication'])} in the replication. Only the unit on the threshold is wrong."),
  NA_character_, NA_character_
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values), as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry),
          entries$entry == seq_len(nrow(entries)))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one expression, so they begin in agreement
# and this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span
# to another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its
# value. Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the
# counts line up, and the spelled form counts as the numeral because entry 3 sets "four".
marked_spans <- function(x) str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2]

inside_span <- function(value, span) {
  numeral <- str_detect(span, fixed(value))
  spelled <- !is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value))) &&
    as.numeric(value) %in% seq_len(12) &&
    str_detect(span, fixed(spell(as.numeric(value))))
  numeral || spelled
}

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values)) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

# Where a span carries two numbers at once the pairing by position is not available, so the
# value is required to be inside some span instead. No entry here is of that shape; the
# branch is what keeps the gate usable on a paper that has one.
placement <- function(values, spans) {
  if (length(values) == length(spans)) {
    map2_lgl(values, spans, inside_span)
  } else {
    map_lgl(values, \(v) any(map_lgl(spans, \(s) inside_span(v, s))))
  }
}

quantified <- quantified |>
  mutate(placed = map2(values, spans, placement))
value_placed <- map_lgl(quantified$placed, all)

# The placement is written to the spine as values_in_spans, one logical per corrected
# value in the same order, so a reader can see it without rerunning this gate.
entries <- entries |>
  left_join(
    quantified |>
      transmute(entry, values_in_spans = map_chr(placed, \(p) str_c(p, collapse = ";"))),
    by = "entry"
  )

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# An entry that changes a quantity has to say which one, and an entry that changes none
# may not carry a value. The class is the declaration and this is where it binds.
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class == "quantity"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class != "quantity"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | !is.na(entries$claim_ids))
)

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it differently.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")

# This note bolds the corrected side only, so the published side is set with its marks
# removed rather than resolved.
plain <- function(x) str_remove_all(x, "\\[\\[|\\]\\]")

# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, which is why every emitted
# entry opens with one.
emit <- function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n> ", plain(e$published),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

This note lists `r spell(nrow(entries))` misstatements in "Do Belief Systems Exhibit Dynamic Constraint?", published in *The Journal of Politics* 84(2), 725--738, doi [10.1086/716294](https://doi.org/10.1086/716294). **None of them changes a conclusion of the article.** The finding that treatments which move a target attitude leave nontarget attitudes untouched is unaffected: the pooled indirect effect is small and statistically indistinguishable from zero on either the published figure or the corrected one, and every estimate in tables 1 through 4 reproduces exactly.

The first two are the same pooled ratio, printed with the wrong sign in the results section and again in the discussion. The next two attach real estimates to the wrong sample. Four more are counts and roundings that disagree with the article's own tables. The last supplies two cross-references the appendix omits.

Every corrected value below is computed from the deposited data at the time this document is rendered; bold marks the tokens that change. The interval endpoints quoted alongside a corrected point estimate are left exactly as the article prints them, because each is one draw of an unseeded bootstrap and every one of them falls inside the range that bootstrap produces. The code and output supporting each correction are at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_green_2022](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_green_2022).

```{r rendered-entries, results="asis"}
walk(entries$entry, emit)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else
# that needs these entries reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot
# drift.
# na = "": a withdrawn entry has no corrected text and an entry that corrects no recorded
# quantity has no claim id, and an empty field says that in every reader. The default writes
# the two letters NA, which a reader outside R takes for text.
# The spine's vocabularies are closed (cleanup of 2026-11-07): a value outside them is a
# typo, and the edition builders read these columns to shape every entry.
stopifnot(
  all(entries$class %in% c("quantity", "description", "interpretation", "definition", "label", "float", "cross_reference", "wording", "spelling", "typography", "bibliographic")),
  all(entries$form %in% c("full", "brief", "note")),
  all(entries$source %in% c("pipeline", "reading", "reference_audit", "publisher_record", "authors_archive", "proof"))
)
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"), na = "")
```
